| [THEORY-045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md) v3 | Felt affect is experience of the regulatory state | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), and Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), are two independent accounts that agree on a base layer. What is felt as affect (valence and arousal for Barrett, feeling for Damasio) is the body's regulatory state. Its valence is that state's value for the organism, and it is present in hunger, pain and well-being as much as in emotion. They disagree about what the experience is of. For Barrett it is the brain's allostatic prediction of the body, issued from agranular limbic cortex. For Damasio it is a topographic map of the body's state, built in the upper brainstem, and their paper makes no use of prediction. Seth ([LIT-135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md)) builds on the same base but makes his claim about consciousness, not about affect. Friston ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) supports neither. Proposed: both sources are theoretical syntheses, and neither tests the claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-059.md) | Readiness potential doesn't show a prior decision | Libet read the readiness potential, which begins half a second or more before a spontaneous movement and before the reported urge, as the brain deciding first. Two independent arguments in the record remove that inference. Schurger, Sitt & Dehaene ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) show that a leaky accumulator driven by noise and fitted to waiting times alone reproduces the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96), because movement-locked averaging recovers the fluctuations that crossed threshold; a prediction of theirs held in 13 people. Dennett & Kinsbourne ([LIT-431](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-431.md)) argue that the clock report times a represented content, not an event in the brain. Proposed: the authors say their model shows the potential could be fluctuation, not that it is. It says nothing about whether the urge causes the act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-062](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-062.md) v2 | Reliability, not a supervisor, arbitrates control | Daw, Niv & Dayan ([LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md)) cast habitual and goal-directed instrumental control as model-free caching and model-based search, and let behaviour follow whichever estimate is less uncertain; simulations reproduce the effects of over-training, task complexity and reward proximity on devaluation. Dayan & Berridge ([LIT-584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-584.md)) show from instant revaluation of a salt cue that Pavlovian prediction also has a model-based form, and suggest the same reliability arbitration there. Both controllers pursue the same ends; neither is the irrational one. The instrumental half is qualitative simulation; the Pavlovian half of the arbitration is a suggestion. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md) v2 | Unity of experience needs no self-model | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md): the globality constraint makes every conscious content part of one world-model. On the functional level that is "highest-order binding" into a single causal role, and on the neural level the prediction of "one single area of maximal causal density", after Tononi and Edelman's dynamic core. "What you subjectively experience upon experiencing your world as coherent is the high internal correlation strength between a subset of physical events in your own brain." A unified world comes before a self: the minimal case is "Selfless Snapshot Consciousness", and fully depersonalized states are "non-subjective consciousness". The neural half is a cited hypothesis, the précis says little is known, and how the cluster becomes one subject's is left open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | Control allocation is a cost-benefit computation | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md) v2 | Cortical slow waves are organized by spirals | Xu, Long, Feng & Gong (2023), [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md): in Human Connectome Project fMRI band-passed to 0.01–0.1 Hz, the cortical phase field holds about 16–19 spirals at a time around phase singularities, concentrated on boundaries between functional regions; their centres drift superdiffusively, opposite spirals annihilate (51% fully, 46% partly) and like ones repel (2.6%), and their positions and senses decode task condition above a raw-amplitude decoder. One source, fMRI only, at a spatial scale chosen because it maximised that decoding; the routing of activity flow is read from phase gradients and a phase-oscillator model, never perturbed. The kinship with Belousov–Zhabotinsky spirals and pattern-formation defects is the record's analogy, not the paper's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) v2 | Basic affective consciousness is subcortical | Newen & Montemayor's ALARM theory (2025), [LIT-626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-626.md): basic arousal, a sensitivity to pain, pleasure and other basic affect without focused attention, can be realised without cortex, by the upper brainstem and thalamus, and its function is to alarm the bodily agent when a homeostatic variable leaves its range, giving the signal "100% weight" through "rather rigid behavioural programmes without choices". Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), supply the subcortical clause independently: feeling is generated in the upper brainstem and the insula is not needed. Both papers argue from cited evidence and offer no new data, and neither has a marker that tells a felt alarm from an unfelt one. The function clause rests on ALARM alone, and Veit's account rivals it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) v2 | Homeostatic feelings make contents conscious | Damasio & Damasio (2022), [LIT-628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-628.md), an essay with no data, read only through a summarising fetch tool, so its wording is paraphrased here. Consciousness is the spontaneous identification of mind contents as belonging to one's own organism, and a continuous stream of homeostatic feelings, from hunger and pain to a faint feeling of existing, supplies it; the feelings are conscious in themselves and confer consciousness on exteroceptive images. They are hybrid because interoceptive axons are unmyelinated, partly non-synaptic and outside a systematic blood–brain barrier, so viscera and circulating molecules act on the neurons that map them. Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), read in full, supply the upper-brainstem site of feeling and the unmyelinated-fibre proposal. Proposed: the identification is a definition, the mechanism an interpretation of anatomy, and the clinical evidence does not separate this account from its rivals. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report isolates the NCC | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-096.md) | Consciousness is global neuronal ignition | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene (2020), [LIT-631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-631.md), a review by the theory's proponents. Conscious access is "a non-linear network ignition" that amplifies and sustains a representation so that local processors can access it, in a distributed core of long-range layer II/III and V pyramidal neurons with prefrontal cortex a key hub but "not ... the exclusive territory". Ignition is exclusive: one content at a time. Evidence: seen and unseen trials diverge after about 200 ms across modalities; in van Vugt et al.'s monkeys, missed stimuli drove V1 and V4 but only reported ones, and false alarms, ignited sustained prefrontal firing, and the signal-detection threshold is the ignition threshold. The review adopts the premise that global availability "is what we subjectively experience as a conscious state", and calls experience without access untested; that premise, not the access data, is where it rivals overflow and the sensory account. Single source, second-hand evidence, and the P3 question conceded open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) | Distant co-ripples carry forebrain coordination | Verzhbinsky, Daume, Cheng, Rutishauser & Halgren (2026), [LIT-633](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-633.md): in 1,373 single units from five bilateral forebrain regions of 35 epilepsy patients doing a Sternberg task, ripples (70–100 Hz, about 70 ms) co-occur between bundles at a median 5% at every tract distance from 71 to 223 mm, and unit pairs co-fire a median 34% more during co-ripples than in no-ripple periods, beyond a rate-only null and with no loss over distance. The gain rises with load (13% in maintenance, 19% at retrieval), and encoding co-firing for a stimulus recurs at retrieval in 0.29% of cell-pair trials in co-ripples against 0.14% outside them. Correlational throughout: one task, two load levels, clinically placed electrodes, nothing perturbed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) v4 | Consciousness is sensory recurrence, not PFC | Block's "back of the head" position, from three papers. Block (2005), [LIT-629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-629.md): a phenomenal NCC (for seen motion, recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal broadcasting), with winner-take-all access letting a recurrent sensory representation lose and stay unaccessed. Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md): the mesh argument. If workspace activation is not part of the basis of experience, strong losing sensory coalitions explain why experience overflows access; if it is, nothing does. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md): no-report designs do not settle the prefrontal question, because thought about the percept persists, and one design that removes it found no prefrontal difference by fMRI, which Block calls evidence against prefrontalism while granting that ECoG could still support it. Proposed: an inference to the best explanation, with every experiment second-hand and the decisive test not yet run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md) | Conscious report correlate needs no laminar cortex | Maldarelli & Güntürkün (2025), [LIT-650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md), reviewing Nieder et al. (2020): in crows reporting near-threshold stimuli, single neurons in the nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL), the functional analogue of prefrontal cortex, fired with the "seen" report whether or not a stimulus was shown and were silent on "not seen" reports. NCL is nuclear, not layered; the cortex-like layers and columns found in birds are confined to the sensory pallium. So a correlate of conscious report does not need laminar cortex. The crow evidence is second-hand, from one laboratory and not in the record, and a report paradigm cannot separate access from phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md) v3 | Ventral code is sustained; prefrontal is transient | Vishne, Gerber, Knight & Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md): in 430 visually responsive subdural electrodes from 10 patients viewing images for 300–1,500 ms with no report on analysed trials, high-frequency activity and single-electrode category selectivity fell about 80% from peak by 800–900 ms, while the pattern across ventral temporal electrodes kept near-ceiling, time-invariant category and exemplar information that ended a fixed delay after the image went off. Prefrontal and parietal information was confined to about 150–600 ms and ignored duration. This met the predictions both IIT's and the global workspace's proponents registered for the paradigm, so it did not discriminate them. Above- threshold images only, sparse right-lateralised frontal coverage, one frequency band; it does not show the code tracks experience rather than input. | Active |
| [THEORY-103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) v3 | Phenomenal experience overflows access | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), and Block (2011), [LIT-640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-640.md). Subjects shown 8–32 items say they see all or almost all of them, report about 4, and when cued after offset can report or compare most of any cued subset: capacity 6–7 of 8 up to 1.5 s (Landman et al.), and 7, 6 and 5 of 8 at 1, 2.5 and 4 s (fragile visual short-term memory), against a working memory that stays at about 4. Block reads the surplus as experienced. The rival "sparse" reading holds it in an unconscious store plus a conscious generic or fragmentary image, and Block argues there is no independent evidence for either posit. Proposed: every experiment is second-hand, and that the surplus is conscious is the contested step. Overflow means most items are unaccessed, not that any is inaccessible. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md) v2 | Selectivity clusters in only 3 of ~20 areas | Posani et al. (2026), [LIT-708](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-708.md): in about 14,000 cortical units of the IBL Brainwide Map, the 8-variable selectivity profiles of 4,617 selective neurons beat a covariance-matched Gaussian null for clustering within a region only in VISp, AUDp and SSp-ul. Elsewhere the profiles form an elongated, unclustered cloud. After merging conditions a region cannot tell apart (leaving 5 to 16 of 16), ≥ 95% of random balanced dichotomies are decodable above a shuffle null in 15 of 16 regions, GU being 0.82. Types do appear when regions are pooled, aligned with anatomy. One task, overtrained mice, a lenient separability criterion. | Active |
| [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md) v3 | Odour statistics look hyperbolic, not Euclidean | Zhou, Smith & Sharpee (2018), [LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md): for strawberry, tomato, blueberry and mouse-urine volatiles, and for Dravnieks' perceptual ratings of 127 odorants, clique-topology Betti curves match a 3D hyperbolic model and reject uniform Euclidean cubes of every dimension tried. It does not show a tree in the data, and because the fitted odour model is a thin shell, it does not separate a hyperbolic metric from a sphere in flat space. | Active |
| [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md) v3 | Place-cell correlations look hyperbolic | Zhang, Rich, Lee & Sharpee (2022), [LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md): in twelve sessions from three data sets, the rank order of CA1 spike correlations matched uniform samples from a 3D hyperbolic ball and not uniform samples from low-dimensional Euclidean cubes or shuffled data, and the ball's radius rose with log exploration time from seconds to days. It does not show that the metric, as opposed to the distribution of field scales, is hyperbolic, nor that a tree is represented. | Active |
| [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md) | Unconsciousness cuts integration at gateways | Luppi et al. (2024), [LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), read in [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md). In resting-state fMRI, the regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones split by rank into gateways (mainly default mode) and broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal). Pairwise ΦR, the whole-minus-sum Φ plus redundancy, falls between default-mode gateways in propofol anaesthesia, in 22 DOC patients, and against post-anaesthetic recovery. The original Φ shows no common decrease. The finding is correlational, pairwise and content-free. The gateway/broadcaster split is imposed by the method; only where its two classes fall is measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md) v4 | Prefrontal cortex carries category, not identity | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). In iEEG and fMRI, with Bayesian support for the nulls, and against a positive control, prefrontal cortex held category but no identity or orientation, and none of 655 prefrontal electrodes showed the onset-and-offset response GNWT predicted. It does not show these dimensions were unaccessed, or that prefrontal cortex lacks them in other signals: high gamma and BOLD only, no single units, and every image was seen. | Active |
| [THEORY-252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-252.md) v2 | On functionalism, idle clamps alter experience | Gidon, Aru and Larkum (2025), [LIT-1000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1000.md), read in full in [NOTE-818](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-818.md): a voltage clamp replaying a recorded response injects no current on the matching stimulus yet fixes the network's transitions on every other, so on the Turing–Putnam definition the computation degenerates while nothing that happens changes. It is a conditional about the view, not evidence about experience; the simulation shows only what an ideal clamp does, and the premise that removing unexercised branches changes experience is cited, not defended. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-261.md) v3 | SDM capacity scales with hard locations | Kanerva (1992), [LIT-921](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-921.md), §§3.5–3.7, read in full in [NOTE-779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-779.md), after Jaeckel (1989a). An approximate derivation for uniform random data and exact retrieval cues. It does not cover noisy cues, which lower capacity, or clustered data, which the uniform design handles badly, and it does not contain the critical-distance analysis that is sometimes attributed to it. | Active |
| [THEORY-262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-262.md) | Complexity peaks with segregated integration | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman (1994), [LIT-998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-998.md), read in [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md). C_N, the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear rise with subset size, is shown low at both extremes for one family of Gaussian matrices, and higher for patchy than for uniform wiring in one simulated visual area and in small linear systems. All of it is simulation. It is a whole-system number over fixed components: it does not find units or boundaries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md) v4 | Hopfield nets recall up to about 0.15N | Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), read in full in [NOTE-819](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-819.md). The energy descent is derived for symmetric couplings; everything quantitative, including the 0.15N figure, the basin width and the merging distance, is simulation at N = 30 and 100. It does not say that spurious states come only from overload: they appear at a low load too. Nor does it say anything about addressed memory. | Active |
| [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) v2 | Precise harm priors can sustain themselves | Linson, Anderson, Markham, Friston & Moutoussis (2025), [LIT-983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-983.md), read in version 2 in [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md). A mechanism shown in illustrative simulation: policy selection by expected information gain, plus a confident prior, withholds the only disambiguating observations, so the prior keeps itself up. Exposure that restores sampling rebalances it; a precision-lowering drug only suppresses symptoms. No data are fitted, parameters are unreported, and the two intervention arms differ in environment as well as mechanism. | Active |
| [THEORY-291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-291.md) | Visceromotor regions form one intrinsic system | Theriault et al. (2025), [LIT-996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-996.md), read in full in [NOTE-761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-761.md), reporting the group's own 3 T (N = 550) and 7 T (N = 90) studies; Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), read in [NOTE-434](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-434.md), for the 3 T system. The anatomy and overlap are reported second-hand. The reading the paper adds, that the named networks' psychological labels are "destined to fail" and that the brain's primary function is allostasis, is not part of this account; the authors themselves do not claim allostasis-first is correct. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-296.md) v4 | No sustained posterior–visual synchronization | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). IIT's proponents predicted sustained gamma-band synchronization between category-selective cortex and V1/V2 throughout a conscious percept. iEEG and MEG phase consistency found only early, brief, 2–25 Hz coupling, mostly evoked, with Bayesian support for the null; exploratory amplitude coupling was also brief. V1/V2 was sparsely sampled in iEEG. It tests IIT's proposed implementation, not integrated information. | Active |
| [THEORY-298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-298.md) | Report can't test posterior sufficiency | Seth & Bayne (2022), [LIT-982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-982.md), "Evaluating theories of consciousness" and Box 3, read in [NOTE-849](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-849.md) from the accepted manuscript. An argument in a review, not a result: the verification of posterior-sufficiency predictions "relies on subjective report …, which in turn requires anterior cortical activity", and validating a non-report marker by theory borrows a contested theory, by introspection, unreliable report. It says the methods are lacking "at present", not that the question is unanswerable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-300.md) | Coercion reduces the sense of agency | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), manuscript pp. 16–17 and Fig. 5, read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md), reporting one experiment by his group (Caspar et al. 2016). Under an experimenter's instruction to press the key that shocked a co-participant, the perceived action–tone interval was longer and the auditory N1 to the tone smaller than under free choice. It shows a reduced experience of agency, not reduced responsibility, and the review says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-302.md) | Action is controlled via coordinative structures | Turvey (1977; read in the 1975 Haskins report), [LIT-904](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), read in [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md). Argued from Bernstein's degrees-of-freedom problem and Greene's equivalence classes, and supported at the spinal level by reflex-probe studies showing the segmental apparatus retuned in the tens of milliseconds before voluntary movement, and by Fel'dman's joint that goes to a preset equilibrium whatever its initial conditions. Its extension to all levels, and to tuning set directly by vision, is the author's speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) | Agency draws on prospective signals too | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md). A review, reporting a binding experiment in which action binding tracked the probability of a tone on trials with no tone, a patient study in which that prospective part was absent in schizophrenia, and priming studies in which ease of action selection raised the sense of control over an outcome it did not predict. It does not say the experience is accurate: the prospective part is by its nature blind to whether control was actually exercised. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) v2 | Ideal-observer stages locate perceptual losses | Geisler (2011), [LIT-1055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1055.md), read in [NOTE-870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-870.md). A review that defines the ideal observer as optimal "given the available information and any specified constraints", and writes it as an expected-utility argmax over the posterior given the stimulus S or a constrained representation Z = g(S;θ). Constraints are added one at a time (optics, receptor sampling and noise, ganglion-cell summation), and human performance that parallels the retinal-stage ideal while falling below it is read as loss in central factors. The empirical parts are the review's account of studies the record has not read. The review gives no formula for efficiency and no notion of an optimum over a restricted class of computations. | Active |
| [THEORY-410](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-410.md) | BCI decoding fits intention–neural identity | Pernu (2018), [LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md), read in [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md). A conceptual argument that turns on an empirical premise the paper asserts and does not examine: that each intention corresponds to one ensemble-average firing value. Real decoders are not simple averages, and whether the mapping holds across sessions or subjects is not checked. It is scoped by its own footnote 1 to difference-making with proportionality. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-454.md) v2 | Percepts enter cognition only when recoded | Block (2024), [LIT-649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md), read in [NOTE-498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-498.md): the précis of his 2023 book, not the book. The main thesis is stated and its arguments are in the book, unread here. The working-memory half is the update: nine cited lines of evidence that working-memory representations differ from perceptual ones and are task-dependent abstractions (moderate). The rereading of the workspace as conceptualisation rather than consciousness is asserted, not argued against the consciousness reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-484.md) | Brain implements options-based hierarchical RL | Botvinick, Niv and Barto (2009), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md), read in [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md). Four proposed extensions of the actor-critic mapping, each matched to existing correlational findings, and predictions the authors say "call for further experimental scrutiny". The evidence for prefrontal coding of subtask segments is "only indirect". The mapping assumes pseudo-reward; other frameworks (HAM, MAXQ) would predict differently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-500.md) | Somatic markers prune options before reasoning | Damasio (1996), [LIT-384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-384.md), read in [NOTE-332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md), the somatic marker hypothesis stated by its author; Bechara, Damasio, Tranel and Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md), the experiment it is usually cited for. The robust result is a group difference: in the gambling task all 10 controls and none of 6 ventromedial patients developed anticipatory skin conductance responses. That controls chose well before they knew, and that the marker causes the choice, is not carried by the statistics. The mechanism is argued, not observed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-529](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-529.md) | Representation is efficient transmission | Martínez (2025), [LIT-149](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-149.md), read in [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md): a position paper with no new theorem or data. Its sharpest point is a standard result: by the data-processing inequality, mutual information about a car/no-car decision can only fall from retina to IT, so a mutual-information criterion would place the decision at the earliest stage; explicitness is better read as ease of decoding. The rest is a proposal supported by selected examples. Complexity has no operational measure, teleofunctions are needed to fix the distortion measure or every system is efficient for some loss, and misrepresentation and engineered systems are not addressed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-571](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-571.md) | Brain states are metastable landscape dynamics | Vohryzek, Cabral, Vuust, Deco & Kringelbach (2022), [LIT-080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md), read in full in [NOTE-054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-054.md). A perspective that reports no data: the landscape (Fig. 6) is illustrative, adapted from earlier work, and no study measures depressed and psychedelic states on a common scale. The psychedelic evidence is small cited studies of broader substate repertoires and higher signal diversity; the depression evidence is three studies, one in remitted patients, though the abstract calls depression "excessively rigid". The modelling section is heavily self-citing. Proposed: a framing, with the record's rival description of the same dynamics as continuous in [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-593](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-593.md) v3 | Perceptual learning can reshape individuation | Ivy & Mroczko-Wąsowicz (2025), [LIT-099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-099.md), read in [NOTE-150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-150.md). A conceptual proposal: a frame is installed by learning, often top-down, and then runs as a perceiver-specific structural principle of objecthood, so the system-level and episode-level questions about cognitive penetration come apart. The support is others' results reread through the concept, and one eye-tracking study of the authors'. The paper does not say what "bottom-up" means once priors sit in early processing, calls a frame "a specific top-down prediction" in §3.iii, and shows different weightings, not different objects. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-603.md) v2 | Iowa task doesn't show pre-aware advantage | Bechara, Damasio, Tranel & Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md). The robust results are the group difference in anticipatory SCRs (Fisher's exact, one-sided P < 0.001) and the insufficiency of stated knowledge in three patients. The abstract's "before they realized which strategy worked best" and "before they knew" outrun notes 8 and 9: the pre-hunch choice preference was not significant, and the pre-hunch SCR effect reported is group × period, with no bad-versus-good deck test. Nothing here shows that the SCR, or what it indexes, causes the choice. | Active |
| [THEORY-618](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-618.md) | Hyperbolic neural geometry evidence is thin | Sharpee (2019), [LIT-875](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md), read in [NOTE-670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md): a four-page programmatic review with no new result, whose reading filed no THEORY because its claims are conjectures. Filed here as Proposed because the record holds two tests of the conjecture, odour statistics ([LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md), [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md)) and CA1 place-cell correlations ([LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md), [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md)), and no general statement. The Zipf step shows a shared exponential count of states, which any system with extensive entropy has, not a shared metric, and the rigidity argument for three dimensions cites Mostow's theorem, which concerns finite-volume manifolds and says nothing about noisy point clouds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-660.md) | Branching minimises surface, not length | Meng, Piazza, Both, Barzel & Barabási (2026), [LIT-069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-069.md), read in full with the SI in [NOTE-075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-075.md). Only two symmetric motifs are solved, each by a local, penalised optimiser started from the Steiner layout; the "exact" mapping to string worldsheets holds for a problem the paper does not solve. The random-terminal prediction is a sigmoid fitted to one tetrahedron, trifurcations are partly made by a merging rule, the one robustness check moves the key statistic 4.3-fold, and the sprouting breakpoints are chosen per dataset with no null. Real motifs are about 25% longer than Steiner, which the model leaves unexplained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) | Two-stage cascade can read signal frequency | Folz, Wettmann, Morigi & Kruse (2018; PRE 2019), [LIT-034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md), read in full in [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md). The period independence is proved, for signals that differ by a time rescaling only; the two-stage readout is shown numerically and in the Heaviside limit; the loop's minimum length and ω ≈ √3 v/L for long axons come from linear stability analysis. The length control is a lumped delay-differential model with one parameter set and the motor velocity v never stated, so its absolute lengths, about 125 µm, cannot be reproduced. A proof of mechanism, not a model fitted to axons. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md) | Attention approximates SDM reads only locally | Bricken & Pehlevan (2021), [LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md), read in full in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), which re-evaluated the intersection formula and the fit. The exact intersection (Eq. 2) is checked against Kanerva's lune formula and simulation; eight SDM and fitted-softmax variants retrieve almost identically on random patterns, MNIST and CIFAR-10, with three named exceptions. The intersection is a staircase in distance, the fit holds to about dv = 20 for d = 15, the analytic β of App. B.2 is about 2–2.5 times too small, and every optimal radius assumes random patterns and addresses. The GPT-2 "confirmation" and the cerebellar implementation of attention are argument, not demonstration. | Active |
| [THEORY-765](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-765.md) v2 | Synchronous brushing induces rubber hand illusion | Botvinick & Cohen (1998), [LIT-1277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md), read in full in [NOTE-1006](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1006.md). Ten subjects affirmed referred touch and ownership after ten minutes of synchronous brushing; after thirty minutes their blind reaches drifted toward the rubber hand in proportion to how long the illusion was reported; asynchronous brushing cut both. It does not show that synchrony alone, apart from expectation, produces the report, and it concerns a hand, not the whole body or the self. | Rejected — Rejected on 2026-10-20 by its own refutation condition: drift toward the rubber hand appeared as strongly under asynchronous brushing interrupted by pauses, and with the hand only seen (Rohde et al. 2011, LIT-1281). Its suggestion control was also too weak to separate perception from expectation (Lush & Seth 2022, LIT-1267). The report half is restated, narrower, in THEORY-766. |
| [THEORY-766](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md) v3 | Rubber hand reports may reflect expectation | Botvinick & Cohen (1998) and four replications read here give a synchrony effect on reports of referred touch and ownership. Rohde et al. (2011) and Abdulkarim & Ehrsson (2016) separate drift from ownership. The suggestion debate (Lush 2020; Lush et al. 2020; Ehrsson et al. 2022; Lush & Seth 2022; Roseboom & Lush 2022) shows that the standard controls do not equalise expectations. The ownership report is weaker than the referred-touch report and tracks trait suggestibility. Whether the synchronous stimulation, not expectation, produces the report difference is not settled. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the report differences measured ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3); the perceptual reading is [THEORY-827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-827.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-767](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-767.md) v2 | Heartbeat signals feed body ownership | Seth (2013), [LIT-1263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1263.md), read in full in [NOTE-1000](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1000.md). An opinion article that reports, at second hand, that a virtual hand pulsing with the heartbeat was owned more (Suzuki et al. 2013, the author's own group), that a virtual body pulsing with it was identified with more (Aspell et al. 2013), and that people with lower heartbeat-detection sensitivity are more susceptible to the rubber hand illusion (Tsakiris et al. 2011). None of the studies was read here, and no control separates the heartbeat from any other periodic signal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-768](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md) v2 | Minimal self is whole-body identification | Blanke & Metzinger (2009), [LIT-1274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1274.md), read in full in [NOTE-1002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1002.md), with Lenggenhager et al. (2007), [LIT-1279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1279.md), read in full in [NOTE-999](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-999.md), for the full-body illusion it leans on. Minimal phenomenal selfhood is given three dimensions: global self-identification, self-location and a weak first-person perspective. Out-of-body experience, heautoscopy and full-body illusions vary them; the rubber hand illusion is said not to. The necessity and sufficiency claims are asserted, and the agency thesis rests on adults whose agency was intact. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-769](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md) v2 | Body ownership is causal inference | Apps & Tsakiris (2014), [LIT-1262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1262.md), read in full in [NOTE-991](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-991.md), with Botvinick & Cohen (1998), [LIT-1277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md), for the illusion it explains. The rubber hand, enfacement and rubber-voice illusions are read as one inference: unimodal surprise from synchronous stimulation is explained away by shifting the probability that a part is "me". The account fits the findings; its authors grant there is little direct evidence and that it is hard to falsify with standard fMRI. It does not say why such a model is experienced as a self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-800](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-800.md) | Hopfield stores ~0.15N; forgetting keeps recent | The large-N and forgetting clauses that [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 051) narrowed it to Hopfield's simulations at N = 30 and 100. Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), expects the 0.15N figure "for all large N" from a crosstalk estimate, and states in words that overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten, with saturating couplings as the mechanism. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-827.md) | Rubber hand illusion isn't driven by expectation | Ehrsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1264.md), read in [NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md), conclude that the rubber hand illusion is a perceptual illusion driven primarily by multisensory mechanisms ([NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md), C8), from the synchrony difference's independence of hypnotisability in Lush et al.'s 353 participants. Lush and Seth's reply, [LIT-1267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1267.md), shows that uniform but unequal expectations predict the same null. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-766](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md), only the report differences and that the standard controls do not equalise expectations. This is the perceptual reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when that narrowing set it aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-830](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-830.md) | Sustained seeing rests on a stable sensory code | Vishne, Gerber, Knight and Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md), read in full in [NOTE-499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-499.md), conclude from their intracranial recordings that sustained visual experience may rest on a stable sensory representation, with frontoparietal representation serving discrete updates, and propose a stable "experience subspace". Their measurement, in ten patients and for images up to 1.5 s, is the Active [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md). This is the general claim that measurement was filed to support, held Proposed until a second method or cohort and a case where percept and input come apart test it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-870](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-870.md) v3 | TM pure-awareness ratings unlinked to EEG | Chandia-Jorquera et al. (2026), [LIT-1354](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1354.md), read in the bioRxiv v3 preprint in [NOTE-1058](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1058.md). 33 practitioners against 33 matched controls who counted: higher and more variable retrospective pure-awareness traces (d = 0.77, 1.32); 65% balanced accuracy separating meditation from counting, on entropy and aperiodic EEG; 88% sensitivity separating meditation from rest, on low-frequency phase coherence. The sharp edge: the authors found no robust association between the reports and the EEG, so this is a finding about a practice period and about reports, not a neural signature of an experience with little content. | Active |
| [THEORY-871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md) v3 | Reappraisal leaves subcortical responses unchanged | Bo et al. (preprint 2023, published 2024), [LIT-1359](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1359.md), read in full from the bioRxiv v2 preprint in [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md). Reported negative affect fell under reappraisal (d = 0.92, n = 358). Every subcortical region engaged by negative pictures, amygdala subregions and PAG included, showed 10:1 evidence of no change under reappraisal, as did most cortical emotion-responsive regions; the eight regions reduced were all cortical. BOLD and one rating per trial; it does not show that the unchanged response is part of what is felt, though the authors write as if it were. | Active |
| [THEORY-873](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-873.md) v2 | Consciousness claims caricature attention | Graziano (2024), [LIT-1358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1358.md), read in full in [NOTE-1071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1071.md): the attention schema theory and its "deep illusionism", in an essay with no new data. Arrow B is an argument. The identification of the target with attention rests on covariation with report cited from others, and the merging of attention, workspace and integration is asserted. Its "small" illusionism keeps the modelled process real and denies the reported phenomenal essence, so it is the strong illusionism of [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) with a named target, not the weak kind. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-878](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-878.md) | Reappraisal partly runs apart from generation | Bo et al. (preprint 2023, published 2024), [LIT-1359](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1359.md), read in full from the bioRxiv v2 preprint in [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md). Two fMRI samples (n = 182 and 176), voxelwise Bayes factors, every effect replicated in both. Sixteen regions are engaged by reappraisal and show 10:1 evidence of no response to negative against neutral pictures without it; fourteen, the larger set, are engaged by both. The selective set best predicts how much reported negative affect falls. One instructed strategy, one stimulus type, BOLD only; nothing shows the selective regions do the regulating. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-880](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-880.md) v2 | Quality space fixes phenomenal character | Lyre (2022), [LIT-1344](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1344.md), read in full in [NOTE-1060](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1060.md): neurophenomenal structuralism as a programme. The thesis is assumed and motivated, not shown. Its neural evidence is one cited imaging study of colour in V4. The reduction it draws rests on metaphysically necessary supervenience, which the author says he cannot argue for. It is filed so that the objections read with it, Negro ([THEORY-868](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-868.md)) and Aldé ([THEORY-867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-867.md)), have a stated target. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-881](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-881.md) | Anaesthesia lowers integrated information ΦR | Luppi et al. (2026), [LIT-1357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1357.md), read in full in [NOTE-1064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1064.md) from the open-access version of record. It extends the same group's 2024 result ([LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md)) from human propofol and disorders of consciousness to four species and six regimes, and adds a causal reversal in two macaques. The sharp edge: the state measured is responsiveness, which the authors call "presumably consciousness" and grant is "an imperfect marker of unconsciousness"; the measure is pairwise, linear-Gaussian and content-free; and one mouse regimen fails the main analysis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-883](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-883.md) | Conscious contents are policy-informing posteriors | Whyte, Corcoran, Robinson, Smith, Moran, Parr, Friston, Seth & Hohwy (2026), [LIT-1364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1364.md), read in full in [NOTE-1062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1062.md) from arXiv v2. The "hard core" the paper reads off the active inference models of rivalry, access, no-report, interoception and meta-awareness. The first two parts follow from the framework; the criterion of access is "an inference to the best explanation" from what the models needed in order to report. The authors scope it to humans and similar animals and are agnostic elsewhere. Neither prediction has been tested in the paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-886](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-886.md) | Prediction error spikes mark event boundaries | Zacks, Speer, Swallow, Braver & Reynolds (2007), [LIT-1382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1382.md), read in full in [NOTE-1084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1084.md) from the PMC author manuscript. Event segmentation theory: a theory and review, with a partial network simulation and mostly correlational evidence. Prediction error is never measured in people, and the one neural prediction checked (anterior cingulate responses at boundaries) failed. It is a theory of a passive observer of others' activity; it does not cover one's own intentions, and does not mention the doorway effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md) v3 | Wanting can rise without liking | Berridge and Kringelbach (2015), read in [NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md). Reward splits into 'liking', 'wanting' and learning. 'Liking' has objective, cross-species orofacial markers. Lateral-hypothalamic stimulation and incentive sensitization raise 'wanting', which can grow "even if the drug became less pleasant". Objective 'liking' reactions can occur "without any subjective pleasure feeling at all". Filed because it bears directly on the record's reading of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-895](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-895.md) v2 | Drugs sensitize wanting, not liking | Berridge and Robinson (2016), [LIT-1461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1461.md), read in [NOTE-1109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1109.md) from the PMC author manuscript. A review by the theory's authors. Strong in rats and moderate in people for drugs; weak for behavioural addictions, where the authors call the evidence emerging and the mechanism unknown. Filed separately from [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md), which holds the liking–wanting dissociation, because what [QUESTION-267](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-267.md) and [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) need is the sensitization result: a ranking whose strength is re-keyed to cues, cut loose from both pleasure and the person's goals, and lasting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-909](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-909.md) v2 | Plasticity needs neuromodulator within seconds | Gerstner, Lehmann, Liakoni, Corneil & Brea (2018), [LIT-1494](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1494.md), read in full from the CC BY version of record in [NOTE-1130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1130.md). A review of five experimental papers, 2014–2017 (Yagishita; He; Brzosko 2015 and 2017; Bittner), not new data. Mostly slices, one laboratory per region; the minute-scale CA1 result may be consolidation. The reviewers grant that other mechanisms could bridge the same gap. | Active |
| [THEORY-923](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md) v2 | One T-maze run: habits persist after devaluation | Friston, FitzGerald, Rigoli, Schwartenbeck, O'Doherty & Pezzulo (2016), [LIT-1476](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1476.md), read in full from the CC BY version of record in [NOTE-1138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1138.md). One simulated T-maze task. The habit is one more policy scored by posterior probability; its prior and transitions grow by count, not by reward. It shows persistence under devaluation, a cached mapping failing when what is appropriate changes; it does not show amortization, and its reaction times are simulation run times. | Active |
| [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md) | dACC specifies control by its expected value | What the expected-value-of-control paper proposes, split from [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) by the sixth status review ([ADR-058](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)'s route) so that a claim needing only the proposal can stand on it. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-446](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-446.md)), so the reading of what it proposes is held. Whether the proposal is true, a fit of the computation and a dissociation of specifying from implementing, stays [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1178.md) | Eligibility traces support three-factor learning | The wide form [THEORY-909](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-909.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-909](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-909.md), Active, is its evidence. Gerstner, Lehmann, Liakoni, Corneil & Brea (2018), [LIT-1494](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1494.md), read five experimental papers as a decaying eligibility trace whose conversion, and direction, a third factor sets, and as support for three-factor rules on behavioural time scales; the evidence is mostly slices, one laboratory per region, and the reviewers grant that other mechanisms could bridge the gap. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1179.md) | Over-precise harm prior blocks its own correction | The wide form [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) held before the eighth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md), Active, is its evidence. Linson et al. (2025), [LIT-983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-983.md), recast post-traumatic stress as lost context disambiguation and offer the loop as its mechanism; their simulations show it once per phenotype, with unreported parameters, and fit no patient data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1191.md) | Active-inference habits persist after devaluation | The wide form [THEORY-923](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-923](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md), Active, is its evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1196.md) | Typeless neurons still separate nearly all splits | The wide form of Posani et al. (2026), [LIT-708](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-708.md), kept here when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed [THEORY-124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md) to what their analysis of the IBL Brainwide Map measured and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that cortical representations are rarely categorical and highly separable. One task, overtrained mice, eight variables and a lenient separability criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1237.md) | Reappraisal leaves subcortical threat response | The wider thesis Bo et al. assert ("subcortical affective processes are less modifiable by reappraisal than previously thought", p. 20), filed beside [THEORY-871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md), Active, holds what their two midlife samples measured under one instructed strategy. Whether the result holds for reappraisal at large is this entry's question, and its promote_when is [THEORY-871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md)'s old condition, without the version-of-record clause. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1241.md) | TM pure awareness reports not tied to EEG | The general form of Chandia-Jorquera et al.'s finding, filed beside [THEORY-870](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-870.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-870](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-870.md), Active, holds what the one study measured; whether practitioners in general report more pure awareness, robustly to demand, and whether EEG separates the practice from other effortless ones, is this entry's question. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1242.md) | Early vision tracks retinal info, losses central | The thesis Geisler's review asserts, filed beside [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) by the status review of 2026-10-30 ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md), Active, holds what the review reports; whether the parallel holds is this entry's question, and none of the primary stage-by-stage studies (Geisler 1989; Banks, Geisler and Bennett 1987) is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1299.md) v2 | Pure awareness models tonic alertness, selflessly | Metzinger (2020), [LIT-1946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1946.md), read in full in [NOTE-1498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1498.md), and Metzinger (2024), [LIT-1943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1943.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1499.md). MPE is "an inner representation of tonic alertness", "non-egoic self-modelling" that "definitely has representational content". In the 2024 sketch it is "a highest-level but nonegoic self-model" of the system's epistemic openness, which "really endows the content generated on all lower-order levels with phenomenality". It is a hypothesis fitted to retrospective reports. It does not say that consciousness needs no model of the system, only that it needs no model of a knowing self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1301.md) | HKB switching raises then lowers phase spread | Sánchez-Cañizares (2026), [LIT-1992](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1992.md), read in full in [NOTE-1506](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1506.md) from the publisher's open-access PDF. Active for the model's behaviour, which this reading checked: the bistability condition \|a\| < 4b analytically, and the rise and fall by re-simulation (20,000 paths). The paper's statement that the spread decreases "to 0" holds without noise and fails at q = 1. It does not say that the model fits the cited EEG data, which the author calls "only qualitative", or that the parameter changes are the mind's ([THEORY-1302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1302.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1302.md) | Mind sets the landscape, not the state | Sánchez-Cañizares (2026), [LIT-1992](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1992.md), read in full in [NOTE-1506](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1506.md). The interpretation is the paper's (pp. 6–7, 18–20); the last clause is this reading's description of the control architecture it implies, from the model and simulation of pp. 8–12, in which the choice between wells is settled by initial condition and noise. Proposed: the paper says IAT* "cannot be tested with empirical results without further assumptions" (p. 7). Bears on [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) and [QUESTION-071](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1312](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1312.md) | Waveform shape can fake phase-amplitude coupling | Donoghue, Schaworonkow and Voytek (2021), [LIT-1999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1999.md), §5 and Fig. 5D–E, read in [NOTE-1529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1529.md) from the PsyArXiv preprint, standing on Kramer et al. 2008 and Cole et al. 2017. Active: checked by a short simulation in which a sharp-peaked 10 Hz wave gave a modulation index of 0.021 between its phase and 25–60 Hz amplitude against 0.0001 for a cosine, and none in a single-harmonic or an 80–250 Hz band. It does not say any particular published PAC is an artefact, nor that broadband coupling far above the harmonics is. | Active |
| [THEORY-1314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1314.md) | Contextual emergence needs a functional boundary | Jennings (2026), [LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), §§4–6, read in [NOTE-1508](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md), with Bishop and Atmanspacher 2006 ([LIT-1987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1987.md)) and Bishop, Silberstein and Pexton 2022 ([LIT-1993](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1993.md)), both unread, for contextual emergence. The boundary condition is the paper's own addition (fn. 15). Proposed, with a sharp edge: the paper's reason that the boundary resists micro redescription is that its properties "are macro-level ones" (p. 20), which is the point at issue, and its neural evidence fits weak emergence too. Bears on [CLAIM-334](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md), whose supervenience premise it denies. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1317](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1317.md) | High gamma coupling to 2–5 Hz tracks attention | Szczepanski et al. (2014), [LIT-1982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1982.md), read in [NOTE-1528](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1528.md) from the publisher's open-access PDF. Active for what it states: the reported counts (123 of 273 electrodes coupled; 55 stronger contralaterally; 28 correlating with RT, r(41) = −0.51 and r(47) = −0.37 in the examples) were checked against the text, and the ERP and power controls are in it. The sharp edge is the causal one: no manipulation of the coupling was made, and the paper's "facilitate" and Jennings's "improve" outrun it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1326.md) | Fixation breaks value ties in hard choices | Voigt (2022), [LIT-1976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1976.md), an Opinion article read in [NOTE-1517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1517.md). The model is the author's "tentative" synthesis, resting mainly on Voigt et al. 2019 (not held) in which fixation duration and dlPFC and precuneus activity predicted later preference change; the causal role of gaze is imported from other studies. Proposed. The sharp edge for its use by Jennings ([THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md)): the attentional step is bottom-up capture by salience, not top-down prefrontal feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1329](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1329.md) | Conflict stirs chaos making choices undetermined | Kane (2009), [LIT-1984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1984.md), p. 39, read in [NOTE-1518](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1518.md). Kane's neural hypothesis, stated without evidence in this paper. Proposed: it is an empirical claim about brains for which the paper gives none, and the record holds nothing that measures it. It is the attribution [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) makes to Kane, now checked against his text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1337](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1337.md) | Band-power effects can be aperiodic 1/f artefacts | Donoghue, Schaworonkow and Voytek (2021), [LIT-1999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1999.md), §§1 and 3, read in [NOTE-1529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1529.md). Active: the spectral argument is elementary (an aperiodic signal has power at all frequencies, and a change in its exponent moves every band), and the simulations and cited cases (the ADHD theta/beta ratio) are in the text. It does not say aperiodic activity is noise without physiological meaning; the paper calls it "a physiologically informative feature". | Active |
| [THEORY-1340](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1340.md) v2 | Task-trained neural subspaces govern from above | Juarrero (2023), [LIT-1995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1995.md), ch. 15 (pp. 223–232), read in [NOTE-1532](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1532.md); the primary studies are not held. The subspaces and their predictive power are the studies' findings as the chapter reports them. That the subspace controls behavior top down, is "the standing cause of the response" (p. 230) and correlates with prior and proximate intentions (pp. 229–231) is the book's reading. Active as Juarrero's reading, read in full and checked. The step from prediction to top-down control is hers, and the evidence reported is dimensionality reduction, prediction and a network simulation, with no intervention on the pattern; that thesis is kept, Proposed, in THEORY-1559, which extends this one. | Active |
| [THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md) v2 | Attention is prioritizing by one's interests | Jennings (2026), [LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), §6, read in [NOTE-1508](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md). The operational half of the paper: what attention is, how it is told from filtering, and how it forms interests. The stalemate mechanism is taken from Voigt 2022 (LIT-1976), registered unread. Held as what the paper proposes; the criterion is inferred, not tested, and the paper reports no data, so whether the account is true is THEORY-1530's. It does not say the subject is contextually emergent ([THEORY-1314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1314.md)) or that attention is the source of a free will. | Active |
| [THEORY-1346](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1346.md) v2 | LFP-size fields phase-lock spikes, not counts | Anastassiou et al. (2011), [LIT-1953](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1953.md), read in [NOTE-1516](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1516.md) from the gwern.net scan at the owner's direction. Active as a statement of what the experiments measured, which the paper reports with sizes, samples and corrected tests. It does not say that the fields neurons generate do this in vivo, that ephaptic coupling bears on attention or experience, or that it is evidence against micro-level description, which is the use Jennings makes of it ([LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), p. 35). | Active |
| [THEORY-1355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1355.md) v2 | Extinction is learned as a new latent cause | Gershman, Blei & Niv (2010), [LIT-2011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2011.md), read in [NOTE-1547](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1547.md). A Chinese restaurant process mixture over trials, inferred online by a particle filter, reproduces acquisition, extinction, ABA and ABC renewal and context-specific latent inhibition in simulation; with the concentration set to zero it reproduces the loss of context-dependence after hippocampal lesions and in young rats. Proposed: the support is qualitative simulation beside replotted data from other labs, with no fitted parameters and no quantitative comparison with rival models. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1364](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1364.md) | Task-set structure shows in prefrontal EEG | Collins, Cavanagh and Frank (2014), [LIT-2007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2007.md), read in [NOTE-1550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1550.md). Proposed: one sample, the participants of Collins and Frank's (2013) Experiment 2 (N = 35; 33 for ERP, 32 for classification), with several uncorrected topographic tests and an early-positivity window chosen from the grand average. The late switch negativity tracked the context dimension but did not predict transfer; the early positivity, absent at group level, and the decoder did (ρ = 0.5, ρ = 0.35), and agreed with each other only marginally. The context dimension is assigned from behavioural switch-costs, so the EEG does not read out the structure independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1530](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1530.md) | Attention breaks stalemates, forming interests | The account Jennings (2026), [LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), proposes, filed beside the Active report [THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md) by the twenty-seventh status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md), [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). The criterion is inferred, not tested, and the stalemate mechanism is taken from one model, Voigt 2022. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1559.md) | Training carves a task subspace guiding behaviour | Juarrero (2023), [LIT-1995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1995.md), ch. 15, read in [NOTE-1532](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1532.md); the thesis the book asserts and [THEORY-1340](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1340.md) reports. The primary studies (Churchland, Cunningham et al. 2012; Shenoy, Kaufman et al. 2011; Kaufman, Churchland et al. 2014; Mante, Sussillo et al. 2013) are not held, and reading them is the first step towards this entry. Proposed: the evidence the chapter reports is dimensionality reduction, prediction and a network simulation, with no intervention on the pattern. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1584.md) v2 | Fans recall plays by allegiance | Botzung et al. (2010), [LIT-1734](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1734.md), read in [NOTE-1313](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1313.md) in place of Talarico and Moore ([LIT-1125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1125.md)). Twenty-three male Duke and UNC fans, an archived game watched three times, 64 clips recalled under fMRI a day later. Fan identification screened participants and was not varied. One game, one-day delay, small sample. | Active |
| [THEORY-1601](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1601.md) v2 | Planarian memory may survive decapitation | Levin and Shomrat (2013), [LIT-1776](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1776.md), read in [NOTE-1283](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1283.md) (marked Skimmed for its thinness, read in full) in place of Shomrat and Levin 2013 ([LIT-1732](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1732.md)). An automated device trained 12 worms at a time, around the clock, scored by computer, to meet the objections to McConnell's hand-run work. No numbers, methods or controls are given, and the store is said to be unknown. | Active |
| [THEORY-1602](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1602.md) v3 | Paternal odour fear passes as odour sensitivity | Dias and Ressler (2014), read in full ([NOTE-1281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1281.md)). The best animal case for [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s germline route, and narrower than it is cited for: cue-specific sensitivity, not inherited fear. IVF offspring were tested for anatomy only, cross-fostering was done on the maternal line only, and the proposed sperm mark rests on groups as small as four. [QUESTION-302](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-302.md) cites it for where an insect's learned aversion would pass to offspring. | Active |
| [THEORY-1607](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1607.md) v2 | Synaptic plasticity alone can't explain memory | Blackiston, Shomrat and Levin (2015), [LIT-1707](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1707.md), read in [NOTE-1258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1258.md). A perspective with no new data. It calls the insect mechanism unsolved and the mushroom-body account indirect, and describes the lobe the 2008 moth paper relied on as partly pruned. Its non-synaptic "blueprint" and its bioelectric store are hypotheses; the planarian evidence is the authors' own one-sentence result and a contested 1960s literature. | Active |
| [THEORY-1634](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1634.md) v2 | Caterpillar odour aversion survives metamorphosis | Blackiston, Silva Casey and Weiss (2008), [LIT-1680](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1680.md), read in [NOTE-1249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1249.md). After fifth-instar odour-shock training, 78% of larvae (N = 41) and 77% of the moths they became (N = 27) avoided ethyl acetate, and 12 of 15 tracked individuals chose alike at both stages. Washing trained pupae or scenting naive ones changed nothing. Third-instar training survived two larval molts (81%, N = 32) and was not expressed by adults (N = 15, a null). The mushroom-body carrier is the authors' hypothesis, not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-1662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1662.md) | Brain sickness responses are pathogen-specific | Sullivan et al., read in [NOTE-1775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1775.md) (Read). In mice, five sterile immune challenges modelling bacterial infection (LPS), viral infection (poly I:C), parasite infection (soluble *Toxoplasma* antigen, STAg), allergy (bee-venom PLA2) and colitis (DSS) produce distinct "sickness states" at three scales: organismal (temperature, food intake, locomotion, metabolism, social behaviour, ultrasonic vocalizations), cellular (whole-brain FOS activity, which a classifier uses to predict the challenge) and molecular (a 940-gene MERFISH atlas of the preoptic and paraventricular hypothalamus). The states cluster: LPS with poly I:C; STAg with DSS; PLA2 apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1688.md) | Tumours hijack the host's nerves | Neuron–tumor crosstalk in cancer: molecular mechanisms and translational advances (Jia, Zhao, Tang, Xie, Huang, Liang, Yang, Wu, Sun, Kwan, Sun, Xu 2026), read in [NOTE-1758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1758.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of cancer neuroscience. Tumours recruit nerves (neurotrophins such as NGF and BDNF, axon-guidance cues, perineural invasion) or, in the brain, integrate into existing circuits through tumour–neuron synapses; nerve signalling, chiefly sympathetic norepinephrine through β-adrenergic receptors, then builds an immunosuppressive microenvironment; nerves also reach the tumour through endocrine and metabolic routes, including the transfer of mitochondria from neurons to cancer cells; and cancer pain feeds a loop that raises sympathetic tone. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1692](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1692.md) | Evidence backs gut contributing to consciousness | Hasler, read in [NOTE-1737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1737.md) (Read). Hasler argues that the enteric nervous system (ENS) is a candidate substrate of consciousness on several leading theories. He separates two "logically independent" theses: the **contributory thesis** (enteric processing makes a large contribution to the one consciousness of the whole animal) and the **partial-subject thesis** (the ENS is a second, far simpler locus of experience whose experiences are not the person's). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1694.md) | Metabolite–brain evidence is mostly preclinical | Ahmed et al. (2022), Microbiota-derived metabolites as drivers of gut–brain communication, read in [NOTE-1767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1767.md) (Skimmed). A review of how gut-microbial metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan/indole derivatives, bile acids, sulfated phenolics and others) influence brain functions through immune, neural and endocrine routes, arranged by neurological function, with a closing assessment of how far human evidence supports the preclinical picture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1702.md) | Maternal dysbiosis linked to pup brain changes | Nakhal et al. (2026), read in [NOTE-1738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1738.md) (Skimmed). Pregnant GAD67-GFP mice (6 control, 6 treated dams) received oral vancomycin (20 mg/kg/day, GD8–GD17) to induce gut dysbiosis. Dams' microbiota lost diversity (Chao1, Shannon; PERMANOVA R² = 0.77). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1710.md) | Protect any data that infers mental states | UNESCO General Conference (2025), read in [NOTE-1790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1790.md) (Skimmed). A human-rights-based instrument covering neurotechnology's whole life cycle, medical and non-medical, and extending to "indirect neural data and non-neural data allowing mental states inferences". Core principles include autonomy (individual and relational) and freedom of thought, protection against manipulation, mental privacy, prior free and informed consent, and specific policy measures for data, employment, consumer products, recommender systems, nudging, sleep marketing, neuromarketing and closed-loop environments. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1718.md) | Maternal cells in fetal brain aid development | Schepanski et al., read in [NOTE-1759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1759.md) (Read). Maternal cells (maternal microchimeric cells, MMc) transfer to the fetus and seed the fetal brain, concentrating in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. By scRNA-seq, brain MMc are mostly microglia, plus T, B, endothelial and neuron-like cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1721.md) | Adaptive DBS raises autonomy concerns | Muñoz et al. (2020), read in [NOTE-1755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1755.md) (Skimmed). Semi-structured interviews with 23 researchers in aDBS trials, thematic analysis. Eight themes, by frequency: data privacy and security (91%), risks and safety (83%), informed consent (74%), automaticity and device programming (65%), patient autonomy and control over stimulation (57%), patient selection (39%), post-trial access (39%), personality and identity (30%). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1877](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1877.md) | Modern Hopfield update is transformer attention | Ramsauer et al. (2020; venue reported as ICLR 2021, unconfirmed), [LIT-2651](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2651.md), read in [NOTE-1952](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1952.md): a continuous modern Hopfield network whose one-step update is softmax attention, with proved convergence, exponential capacity for random patterns and one-step retrieval for separated ones. The theorems are carried as stated; the proofs, in a roughly 90-page appendix, were not read. It says what one attention step computes, not that trained keys act as attractors. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1885](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1885.md) | Diffusive routes predict evoked potential spread | Seguin, Jedynak, David, Mansour L, Sporns & Zalesky (2023), read as the bioRxiv preprint in [NOTE-1969](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1969.md). CCEPs from 29,055 stimulations in 550 patients against communication measures on a normative connectome. Search information and communicability rank first among network measures, and they beat direct structural weights even for connected pairs. Distance, search information and FC give an out-of-sample R² of 54% for response probability. All figures are the preprint's. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1887](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1887.md) | One nonlinear synapse can gate effective links | Randi & Leifer (2021), read in [NOTE-1962](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1962.md). The connected response F_ij(t,t′) equals the linear resolvent plus a correction through the nonlinear edges (Eq. 5). In toy circuits inspired by C. elegans, a sigmoidal edge gates transmission, and moderate drive turns a connection into a fractional-derivative-like kernel, while saturation removes the effect. Simulation only; the supplement is unread. A neural instance of [TERM-090](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-090.md)'s memory kernel. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1891](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1891.md) | Neural standing waves explain frequency tuning | Gepshtein, Pawar, Kwon, Savel'ev & Albright (2022), read in [NOTE-1984](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1984.md). A 1-D Wilson–Cowan chain whose point response is a standing, damped wave of intrinsic period. Linear interference sets tuning and lateral modulation and predicts a nonmonotonic TF–SF dependence that reanalysed MT data show. The waves do not propagate. Linearity holds at low contrast, and contrast dependence needs the nonlinear regime.
