Di Volo & Férézou ([LIT-2654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2654.md)) find colliding cortical waves sum sub-linearly. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1895](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1895.md) | Colliding cortical waves sum sub-linearly | Di Volo & Férézou (2021), read in [NOTE-1976](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1976.md). VSD imaging in six anaesthetised mice and a 2-D E/I mean-field model with excitatory coupling inferred per animal. The model predicted, and the data showed, sub-linear summation of waves from C4 and then C2 (10 ms apart): a suppressive wave with a mean peak at about −30%. The main result, and a limit on reading cortical wave interaction as linear interference. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1907](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1907.md) | Single-trial V1 responses are travelling waves | Muller, Reynaud, Chavane & Destexhe (2014), read in [NOTE-1963](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1963.md). VSD imaging in two awake macaques. Waves on 32 of 40 trials in the main session, at 0.25–1.35 m/s, with phase variability flat across distance as a fixed-delay horizontal-fibre network gives. Independent waves in V2 do not cross the areal border. The mechanism rests on a 1-D model, and the detection criterion builds in the speed window. Radial waves, not spirals, so no bearing on [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2002.md) | Structure learning's problem is generating models | From the reading of [LIT-2835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2835.md) in [NOTE-2092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2092.md). Neacsu, So, Rutar, da Costa, Adams and Friston (2026), Minds and Machines 36:33, DOI 10.1007/s11023-026-09787-8 (open access). A conceptual review. It surveys what "structure learning" means across developmental, cognitive and machine-learning work, then defines Structure Learning in active inference as offline Bayesian model selection by model evidence, by refitting or by Bayesian model reduction or expansion. It names the open problem as generating the hypothesis space, not choosing within it. It reports no results. Here because the exchange called it the most useful single paper for what the free-energy literature covers. It maps that literature fairly but leaves active, data-choosing structure learning to [LIT-2815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2815.md). It agrees with [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md)'s framing that reduction, not expansion, is the open half. Read in its NOTE (skimmed in part). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2014](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2014.md) | Fibration breaking is imposed, not predicted | Gili, Avila, Pasquini, Holodny, Phillips, Boldi, Gabrielli, Caldarelli, Zimmer and Makse ([LIT-2804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2804.md)), read in [NOTE-2111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2111.md). A mixed-integer program deletes the fewest tracts from a baseline connectome (five fibres, each an orbit) until each state's observed synchrony clusters are its coarsest balanced colouring. Rest gives four fibres, both tasks five, all with only the identity automorphism, and the rest and task partitions are not ordered by refinement. The account applies [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md): synchrony classes without symmetry. It goes past that theorem in calling an invariant partition "proven to be synchronous", and it predicts no partition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2016.md) | Structure info gain speeds rule discovery | From the reading of [LIT-2815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2815.md) in [NOTE-2105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2105.md). Friston, Da Costa, Tschantz, Heins, Buckley, Verbelen and Parr (2026), Nature Communications 17:10125, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-77209-5 (open access). The paper adds to active inference's expected free energy an expected information gain over model structures. It computes that gain by Bayesian model reduction over a hypothesis space fixed in advance by symmetry priors (81 rules in a three-ball task), so the agent chooses the observations that best discriminate rules. In 64 simulated games the rule was found in a modal 14 trials. Without information gain about half the games failed. It assumes the rest of the generative model is known. Here because the exchange named it as prior art for structure learning beside [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md). It qualifies that entry without meeting its promote_when, and it shows the mechanism [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md)'s sentry would block. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2021.md) | Travelling waves carry global shape information | From the reading of [LIT-2836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2836.md) in [NOTE-2133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2133.md). Jacobs, Budzinski, Muller, Ba and Keller (2025), arXiv 2502.06034. Recurrent networks with only local encoders and local recurrence learn to propagate travelling waves that bring whole-shape information to each pixel; reading each neuron's activity over time, rather than its last state, lets them segment images that need global context, beating feed-forward CNNs of matched receptive field and, on Multi-MNIST, U-Nets of similar size. The motivation is Kac's "hearing the shape of a drum", and a wave RNN reproduces square drums' fundamental frequencies; even an unbiased convolutional LSTM learns waves. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" listed it beside Keller et al. as a way learned systems carry information ([QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md)), and [LIT-647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-647.md) mentions it. The role of the waves rests on comparisons and a training- time correlation, not on intervention. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2026.md) | Pinwheel density is π per hypercolumn | From the reading of [LIT-2807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2807.md) in [NOTE-2109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2109.md). Kaschube, Schnabel and Wolf (2008), arXiv 0801.3651. In a Swift-Hohenberg-type model of orientation-map development dominated by long-range interactions, the density of pinwheels (±1/2 point defects of the orientation map) per hypercolumn tends to exactly π as the interaction range grows and stays near π for intermediate ranges, while in rival models pinwheels annihilate or crystallize. Registered as a stand-in for Kaschube et al. (2010, [LIT-2812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2812.md)), which is Unfetched: it restates that paper's model prediction, not its cross-species measurements. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" cited pinwheels as defect- like singularities that need not be functional units (QUESTION- tmpcb0bf); the paper treats them only as countable markers and assigns no function. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2029.md) | Hint-seeking falls as the agent learns | From the reading of [LIT-2827](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2827.md) in [NOTE-2117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2117.md). Smith, Friston and Whyte (2022), Journal of Mathematical Psychology 107, 102632, DOI 10.1016/j.jmp.2021.102632 (open access; PMC8956124). A practical tutorial on discrete-state active inference: building POMDPs, simulating with SPM's routines, Dirichlet learning and its novelty term, the neural process theory, hierarchical models, and fitting models to choices with recoverability checks and Bayesian model comparison. Its running example is an explore–exploit task with a costly hint. There information-seeking fades as Dirichlet counts grow, falls as the preference for the larger win sharpens, and returns after surprises. Here because the exchange recommended it as the first reading for U31. It is a ready template for the Bayesian baseline and the fitting of [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md), though it has no second process with authority over action and no structure learning. Read in its NOTE (skimmed in part). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2048.md) | Travelling waves extend RNN memory | From the reading of [LIT-2834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2834.md) in [NOTE-2132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2132.md). Keller, Muller, Sejnowski and Welling (2024), ICLR 2024, arXiv 2309.08045. A recurrent network whose recurrence is a ring convolution initialised as a one-step shift (the Wave-RNN) carries travelling waves in its hidden state, and against a matched wave-free network (the identity-initialised RNN) it learns faster and keeps inputs far longer: more than five orders of magnitude lower loss on the copy task, the adding task solved at length 1000, and much more input information retained with the recurrence frozen. The authors read the wave field as a register in which propagation stops later inputs overwriting earlier ones; randomly initialised local recurrences learn waves in training. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" listed it among ways learned systems keep information through time ([QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md)), and [LIT-647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-647.md) mentions it. The evidence is comparative across models, with no intervention on the waves themselves. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2088.md) | Shared task structure speeds new associations | From the reading of [LIT-2881](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2881.md) in [NOTE-2171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2171.md). A learned shared structure lowers later problems' cost, and barring its use removes the saving. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2090.md) | RNNs reuse dynamical motifs across tasks | From the reading of [LIT-2876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2876.md) in [NOTE-2167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2167.md). Reuse of learned components lowers a later task's cost in RNNs; the transferred component is not intervened on. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2091.md) | Primitive pretraining gives zero-shot rule use | From the reading of [LIT-2877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2877.md) in [NOTE-2170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2170.md). Learned primitives make compositions cheaper, pretraining counted; mechanism correlational. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2098.md) | Consciousness is affective, born in the brainstem | From the reading of [LIT-2891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2891.md) in [NOTE-2186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2186.md), a stand-in for [LIT-2916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2916.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2115.md) | Consciousness theories are meat-neutral | From the reading of [LIT-2925](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2925.md) in [NOTE-2204](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2204.md). An opinion piece. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2168.md) | Integration time moves optimum off criticality | Azizpour and colleagues, [LIT-2980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2980.md), read in [NOTE-2259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2259.md). "Criticality maximizes dynamic range" (Kinouchi and Copelli, [LIT-3027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3027.md)) becomes "only for infinite integration time": every finite readout window has a subcritical optimum, different for the two measures. One transition (branching), one task family (discriminating stationary input rates); the paper itself says the side of the optimum depends on the task and the transition. Grounds [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md)'s window- and task-dependence ([ARG-163](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-163.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2174.md) | V1 eigenspectrum follows a 1/n power law | Stringer and colleagues, [LIT-2972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2972.md), read in [NOTE-2257](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2257.md). V1's code of natural images sits just on the smooth side of the critical exponent 1 + 2/d: a spectrum decaying more slowly would put so much variance in fine directions that the code would stop being differentiable. The bound is strict and asymptotic in rank. It grounds [CLAIM-848](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-848.md)'s premise in that corrected form ([ARG-169](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-169.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2204.md) | Random networks compute best near chaos line | The NIPS 2004 companion ([LIT-3058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3058.md)) of Bertschinger and Natschläger's Neural Computation paper ([LIT-2991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2991.md), unreachable), read in its place in [NOTE-2288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2288.md). The edge of chaos here is a damage-spreading line, K·P_bf = 1, crossing a wide range of mean activity; order is fading memory, and chaos fails because the state carries "spurious" information about initial conditions. The optimum is averaged over many tasks by design, with no per-task optima, so it qualifies rather than defeats [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md) ([ARG-196](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-196.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2209.md) | Ketamine raises approach under threat | Vestring et al. (2026), [LIT-3079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3079.md), read in [NOTE-2300](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2300.md). The nearest design of a second kind that [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found: a drug intervention on the arbitration of approach and avoidance with the objective threat fixed. The represented threat is not measured. Proposed until replicated with the session order counterbalanced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2227.md) | Frontoparietal rivalry activity tracks report | Brascamp, Blake and Knapen (2015), [LIT-3089](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3089.md), read in [NOTE-2317](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2317.md). Rivalry between two dot fields identical except for the eye they reach: switches occur, by matched alternation statistics, but are detected at chance; the fronto-parietal switch response then matches an eighth of the conspicuous response, with no causal remainder. It is the inconspicuous contrast [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) names and supports that account's diagnosis for switch transients. Limit: BOLD and a switch transient, not percept-specific content, and six observers; it separates a perceptual change from awareness of the change, not experience from access. Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2228.md) | Prefrontal cortex tracks no-report rivalry | Kapoor, Dwarakanath, Safavi, Werner, Besserve, Panagiotaropoulos and Logothetis (2022), [LIT-3094](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3094.md), read in [NOTE-2318](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2318.md). 987 prefrontal units in two macaques, percept inferred from the optokinetic nystagmus, decoding up to 95%. It is report-free intracranial evidence that the content reaches prefrontal cortex. Limit: the switches were noticed ("unreported but clearly occurring"), so it does not remove post-perceptual cognition, and it neither promotes nor refutes [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md). Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2229.md) | Split-brain splits perception, not responses | de Haan et al. (2020), [LIT-3102](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3102.md), read in [NOTE-2319](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2319.md) as a stand-in for Pinto et al. 2017 ([LIT-3091](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3091.md)). "Perception appears to be more split, while responding remains largely unified"; "the body of evidence is insufficient" on the subject. It is independent evidence for the access half of [CLAIM-003](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-003.md) in a disconnected brain, argued in [ARG-202](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-202.md). Limit: a review, behavioural evidence, a lesioned brain, and no removal of post-perceptual cognition. Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) | Frontal tDCS raises mind-wandering | Axelrod, Rees, Lavidor and Bar (2015), [LIT-3135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3135.md), read in [NOTE-2357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2357.md). Two small experiments (n = 14 and 31). The causal clause is the authors' inference; the executive-capacity clause rests on a non-significant rise in target detection. The effect was replicated by the first author ([THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md)) and not in a pre-registered three-lab study ([THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md)), so the two accounts rival. It does not say that the stimulation changed the agent's awareness of its own thought or control, which was not measured, and so it is not a test of Metzinger's H1, which the 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), p. 14) cited it for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md) | tDCS mind-wandering effect bypasses meta-awareness | Axelrod, Zhu and Qiu (2018), [LIT-3134](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3134.md), read in [NOTE-2355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2355.md): a direct replication of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment (n = 85) with a meta-awareness probe added. The second clause is the authors' inference, that "at least in some cases mind-wandering might not be regulated by meta-awareness". It rivals the pre-registered null of [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md). For the record it is the nearest the literature comes to Metzinger's H1, and it is not a test of it: the rated awareness is of attention's location, not of the capacity to end a thought, and it was not manipulated. It bears on [QUESTION-367](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-367.md) only as weak evidence that the rate of mind-wandering can move while the agent's self-rating does not. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md) | Frontal tDCS fails to raise mind-wandering | Boayue and ten colleagues (2019/2020), [LIT-3133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3133.md), read from the authors' preprint in [NOTE-2358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2358.md): a pre-registered three-lab replication (n = 192) of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment, with d = -0.11 (HDI [-0.38, 0.17]), BF 10.65 for the null against a positive effect, and a replication Bayes factor of 0.002. The false-positive clause is the authors' inference. It rivals [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) and the first author's positive replication, [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md), which it predates and does not discuss. Whether it corrects [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) is left to the owner. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2277.md) | PTSD delays first gaze to background context | Zidda, Steiger-White, Winkelmann, Ruttorf, Andoh, Nees & Flor (2025), [LIT-3174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3174.md), read in full in [NOTE-2406](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2406.md). A gaze bias against the context of a trauma cue, specific to PTSD against trauma-exposed controls, measured only as the latency of the first look, and tied to poorer relational memory. The nearest study found to the first half of [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md); it has no recall manipulation, and its background does not disambiguate. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2279.md) | Metastability is dynamics, not noise switching | Hancock, Rosas, Luppi, Zhang, Mediano, Cabral, Deco, Kringelbach, Breakspear, Kelso and Turkheimer (2024), [LIT-2266](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2266.md), skimmed from the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-2373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2373.md). A review; the definition and the catalogue of routes are its own synthesis of the literature, the dwell-time test a proposal with computational support. It bears on [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) by separating escape over a barrier by noise from passage near saddles. Proposed until the definition is confirmed in another source. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2284.md) | PTSD gaze lingers on trauma; rest is thin | Diotaiuti, Spica, Di Siena, Cavicchiolo, De Souza, Andrade & Mancone (2026), [LIT-3179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3179.md), read in full in [NOTE-2382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2382.md). A map of what the eye-tracking literature on PTSD has measured. For [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md) it is a check on absence: no included study measures gaze after cued recall, and the use of gaze to track engagement with corrective context in exposure is called hypothetical. The last clause of the title is the reader's count from the review's Table 1, not a sentence of the review. The corpus misses at least two eligible studies. Proposed until an independent search agrees. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2288.md) | Interaction self-organizes across layers | Müller (2026), [LIT-2252](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2252.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2402.md). A hypothesis with stated predictions, supported so far by examples. It reads Haken's enslavement causally, where Schmietendorf ([THEORY-2292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2292.md)) cautions that the slaving principle supports by itself only a descriptive reading. Notes on [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) and [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), no edges. Proposed until its predictions are tested; the promote_when asks for intervention evidence for the constraint it names. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2291.md) | Hierarchical modularity alone yields chimeras | Caprioglio and Berthouze (2024), [LIT-2241](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2241.md), read in [NOTE-2372](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2372.md) (appendices skipped). Numerical, one network family, N = 512. It corroborates [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s first half with its version-5 condition, a gap between levels large against the spread within, and [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md)'s gap-isolated block as the unit; and it bears on [QUESTION-391](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-391.md), since the coarse-grained description fails as the gap closes. | [THEORY-2301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2301.md) | Multiscale posture reveals slow behaviour states | Kaur, Jain and Berman (2026), [LIT-2257](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2257.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2399](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2399.md).
